newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline steady in quiet trade, ARA seen tight.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline steady in quiet trade, ARA seen tight.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices held steady in quiet trade on Thursday.

Traders said supplies were relatively tight in ARA and firmer U.S. Gulf coast markets mainly because of refiner buying ahead of pipeline scheduling and that, rather than Wednesday's U.S. stock draw, supported barge and cargo prices.

However, both barges and cargoes talked in a slightly wider range with a shortage of fixed offers keeping the market notional. Arbitrage opportunities to the United States were not considered workable because of the lack of cargo-sized pieces in Northwest Europe.
A public holiday in Germany also dampened barge demand.
Prompt lifting Eurograde barges were talked around $203/$205 fob ARA with Regular valued slightly firmer at $197.
Eurograde cargo talk was thin but prices edge up on the back of firmer U.S. markets to value around $215 a tonne.
Wednesdays API report showed U.S. gasoline stock off 1.1 million barrels and down around eight million barrels from this time last year although RFG stocks rose 1.35 million barrels last week.
